v.why: Replacing a removed direct edge with a 3x3 conv adds a whole new path, a larger gain than swapping one existing op for another.
Filling an empty edge into the output with a conv restores the input path and yields a bigger gain than replacing an existing op.
Reconnecting node 1 to the input with a conv matters more than upgrading an existing op.
Adding a conv where the edge was missing gives a large gain from the new path.
Replacing none with a conv adds capacity and connectivity, more than replacing another op.
A skip in place of none adds a direct gradient path, which helps more than replacing a pool or conv.
With a direct skip path already present, an extra conv on edge 5 brings diminishing returns.
Removing edge 0 when edge 1 is also none leaves fewer routes from the input and risks disconnecting the cell.
Without the direct 0->3 edge, the paths through node 1 carry more of the signal, so a conv there matters more.
Adding a conv on the 1->2 edge where none existed deepens the path, more than replacing an existing op.
